clue.text: Wood panels found in carts and bed

parts.note: a wain is an old word for a farm cart, so carts are wains
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Someone discovers wooden boards stashed among wagons and a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Wainscoting is the wooden panelling lining the lower part of a room's walls.

clue.text: Like Hook and his sound beginning

definitions.note: the breathy h sound that opens the word 'his'

parts.note: like means as, in the sense 'in the manner of'
Captain Hook is the pirate in Peter Pan

explanation.surface: A description of Captain Hook and how he sounds when he opens his mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like Hook' reads AS PIRATE; the definition is the sound at the start of 'his', the breathed h which phoneticians call by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics the h sound, a puff of breath, is the classic example of this kind of consonant.

clue.text: Jackanory versery perhaps?

parts.note: Jackanory was a BBC children's storytelling programme; a playful 'versery' version would be rhymes for the nursery, like Jack and Jill

explanation.surface: A jokey made-up word suggesting a children's TV story show done in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Jackanory was a long-running British children's TV programme of storytelling; 'versery' blends verse and nursery, and Jack features in many such rhymes.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional children's verse such as Jack and Jill is a typical example of the category.

clue.text: Dealing with building work

definitions.meaning: managing or handling a difficult situation
the capping course of stone or brick along the top of a wall

explanation.surface: Handling construction work on a site.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense means managing successfully; the other is the protective top layer laid on a wall.

clue.text: Spare money to keep hospital

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so the money word holds the hospital letter

parts.note: tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: Spare cash is set aside to fund a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare as an adjective describing a person means lean or slim.

clue.text: Welcome good pair of workers in stables

parts.note: a stable lad and a stable hand are both workers in stables
a stable lad and a stable hand are both workers in stables

explanation.surface: A greeting extended to two capable staff at a riding yard.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase supplies two pieces: both words for workers can follow 'stable' in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To greet someone effusively, often insincerely, as a politician does with handshakes.

clue.text: Chicken seen in this grocery store?

definitions.meaning: a hen house or pen where chickens are kept
the ... is a British chain of grocery shops run by a cooperative society

explanation.surface: A shopper wonders whether poultry is on sale in this food shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The Co-op is a well-known British supermarket chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen enclosure and the British grocery chain share the same spelling.

clue.text: Good person to encourage top person in a party

parts.note: ST, short for saint, is a good person
to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: A worthy individual cheers on the leader of a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicola Sturgeon led the Scottish National Party and was Scotland's First Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicola Sturgeon was leader of the SNP, so she was the top figure in a political party.

clue.text: Her pilot crashes in flying base

indicators.note: a plane that crashes is wrecked, so the letters of the two words are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman's aircraft comes down while flying.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing and take-off site for helicopters is a base for flying craft.

clue.text: Return blows to practise boxing

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word for blows is read from its end

parts.note: raps are sharp knocks or blows

explanation.surface: Hitting back at an opponent while training in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparring is boxing practice with a partner, without full force.

clue.text: Bather uncovered New York pickpocket after swindle

indicators.note: the city and the thief are placed after the swindle word

parts.note: to skin someone is to fleece or swindle them
a dipper is slang for a pickpocket

explanation.surface: A swimmer exposes a thief from Manhattan following a con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' looks like 'exposed', a verb about the pickpocket, but it belongs with 'Bather' in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone swimming with no clothes on is a naked bather.

clue.text: Reworked pastor's ideal religious text

indicators.note: something reworked has been revised and remade, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A minister's ideal has been revised for a sacred document.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'pastor's' counts as a letter of the fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's epic poem on the Fall of Man is a work with a biblical, religious subject.

clue.text: Baltic capital left behind crazy song

indicators.note: the capital and the left letter come behind, that is after, the crazy word

parts.note: mad means crazy
Riga is the capital of Latvia, on the Baltic

explanation.surface: A mad tune left behind in Latvia's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A part-song for several voices, popular in the Renaissance, is a type of song.

clue.text: One carries burden Oriental priest mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the priest's word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk or priest

explanation.surface: A burdened Eastern cleric is referred to.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American animal is used as a pack beast carrying loads.

clue.text: Wear down a sharp point with energy

parts.note: a brad is a thin, pointed nail
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A pointed tip used vigorously to erode a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrape or rub away a surface is to erode it by friction.

clue.text: Rump cooked rare

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters have been worked over and changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A rump steak served underdone.
explanation.definitionFit: The rump of an animal is its hindquarters or backside.

clue.text: End of Star Trek coy about its technology

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter
about suggests the letters are moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: Star Trek is shy about its spacecraft science.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals an anagram of TREKCOY, giving OCKETRY.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of propelling craft by rocket is the space technology Star Trek depends on.

clue.text: Black Country is dull

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a land is a country

explanation.surface: The Black Country, an industrial area of the English Midlands, is said to be boring.
explanation.walkthrough: The Black Country is a once heavily industrial region west of Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without flavour or interest is uninspiring and dull.

clue.text: Group I bring to court for gang crimes

parts.note: a band is a group
to try someone is to bring them before a court

explanation.surface: A prosecutor says they'll take a group to court for gangland offences.
explanation.definitionFit: Robbery and lawlessness by armed outlaws are the crimes of gangs.

clue.text: Mild expletive from martial arts expert about right

indicators.note: the expert's word goes about, or around, the right letter

parts.note: a dan is a grade of black belt in judo or karate, or a holder of it

explanation.surface: A gentle curse uttered by a karate black belt concerning what's correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A softened swear word used in place of 'damn' is a mild oath.

clue.text: Fascinating old fighter meeting one in boxing venue

indicators.note: in places the joined pieces inside the boxing venue word

parts.note: a boxing match takes place in a ring

indicators.note: meeting joins the one letter to the fighter word side by side

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a vet is short for veteran, an old soldier

explanation.surface: An enthralling bout as a retired boxer meets someone in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gripping and absorbing holds attention, like being fixed in place.

clue.text: Gorge last of curry brought in by member of the clergy

indicators.note: the curry's final letter is brought into the clergy word

parts.note: a canon is a cathedral clergyman

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A cleric fetches in the final portion of a curry to eat greedily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gorge' wants to be the verb about eating, but it is the noun for a ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep, narrow valley with steep sides is a ravine or gorge.

clue.text: Bond — that man's in a downward career trajectory

indicators.note: the he's letters go inside the other pieces

parts.note: a dive is a steep downward plunge
that man's is short for 'he's', that man is

explanation.surface: James Bond's career is apparently going downhill fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' looks like James Bond, but it is glue.
explanation.definitionFit: Glue makes things stick, forming a bond between surfaces.

clue.text: Rabbit not caught leading Wonderland character

indicators.note: not means without, so the caught letter is dropped
leading shows the letter dropped is the one at the front

parts.note: to rabbit on is to chatter
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: The White Rabbit, uncaptured, heads the cast of Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' suggests the White Rabbit, but it is the verb meaning to talk endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mad Hatter of the tea party is a figure in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.

clue.text: Refined male, expert in avant-garde

indicators.note: refined suggests the letters are processed and reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: A cultured man skilled in the cutting-edge arts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refined' looks like a description of the man, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Innovative, boundary-pushing art is new and untried, like a trial.

clue.text: Pole position

definitions.meaning: an upright stake fixed in the ground

explanation.surface: Pole position, the front of the grid in motor racing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an upright stake and a job or appointment.

clue.text: Charms eroded initially for old lovers

indicators.note: eroded means worn away, and initially says it is the first letter that goes

parts.note: hexes are spells or charms

explanation.surface: Former partners' appeal fading at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Former partners or spouses are commonly called by this short informal plural.

clue.text: Pass over old American university

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Skipping a venerable US college.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave out or skip something is to pass it over.

clue.text: Means to help about spring

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a spring is the source of a stream

explanation.surface: Ways of helping out around springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season, but it is a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: A supply or asset that can be drawn on for support is a means of help.

clue.text: Long-term plan to get lost sheep caught

indicators.note: the sheep word is caught inside the lost word

parts.note: a stray is lost; stray as an adjective means lost
a teg is a sheep in its second year

explanation.surface: A shepherd's scheme for capturing a straying sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: TEG is a farming word for a two-year-old sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A planned approach to reaching a goal over time is a strategy.
